sentences.text: The species is known only from a single partial skull fossil, MNHN Nr. SVT 331, which preserves the snout and eye regions.
Its skull is the largest known Early Triassic ichthyosaur skull, measuring an estimated 50 cm in length.
The genus Quasianosteosaurus was first named by Maisch and Matzke in 2003.
The fossil was collected from the Sticky Keep Formation at Mount Viking in the Sassendalen area.
Phylogenetic analysis classifies Quasianosteosaurus as a basal ichthyosaur that is the sister taxon to Hueneosauria.
The genus belongs to the family Quasianosteosauridae.
This basal ichthyosaur lived during the late Early Triassic in Spitsbergen, part of the Svalbard archipelago in Norway.
